summary: Canonical security reference for reaching the studio from another device without exposing it to the open internet. Remote access is off by default, driven only from Settings greater than Remote access never a terminal, with two independent modes: Tailscale private encrypted tailnet link and LAN connect-code plus per-device approval on the local network. Containers and SSH forwarding use the printed startup receipt with Studio port and optional sandbox port; browsing the server IP is refused by the trusted Host gate; one-port is enough for ordinary Studio work but both ports are required for Lua and regex benches; this guidance does not broaden hostAllowed or weaken token Origin checks. Two listeners one trust boundary: trusted 127.0.0.1 default 8321 with Host Origin and per-launch session token; untrusted 127.0.0.1:8788 only for the Tailscale sidecar with per-boot shared secret required on untrusted and refused on trusted. Tailscale owner gate admits only the studio owner's numeric user id fail closed. LAN gate uses CSPRNG connect code argon2id hashed never sent, per-IP throttle, pending approval with caps and 15 minute TTL, self-signed TLS; session cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax without Secure. Host-only surface blocks remote management, open, shutdown, restart, and settings writes. Owner can kick devices. The sidecar is not bundled: three locations are checked, and none reports the unavailable phase rather than a dead Enable control. The aux package fetches it from a release asset, verified against a baked SHA-256 pin before any bytes land. Sidecar lifecycle exits on parent death and kills orphans. What is proven lists unit tests and live end-to-end verification.

sections.title: Containers and SSH forwarding
sections.summary: Container or headless use does not need a browser inside that environment. The hoplight ui startup receipt prints the local Studio URL, one copyable SSH command for the Studio port, and when the isolated Lua regex listener started a second forward for its random sandbox port. Run it on the browser machine, replace user@server, keep the tunnel open, browse localhost with the printed ui-port. Browsing the server or container IP is refused by the trusted Host gate. HTML may arrive before api/settings is refused, so the browser turns that 403 into localhost and SSH instructions with Studio, Settings Remote access deep link, and one-port recovery copy buttons; host-only API gates still decide whether controls may change anything. One-port is enough for ordinary Studio work; Lua and regex benches need both ports because ADR-009 uses a second ephemeral loopback origin. Tailscale and LAN serve the approved Studio surface only and do not make the sandbox listener a general remote endpoint. This does not broaden hostAllowed, expose a new listener, or weaken token and Origin checks.

sections.title: Two listeners, one trust boundary
sections.summary: The app binds two loopback listeners in server-remote and server. Trusted 127.0.0.1 port default 8321 is the local owner's browser, gated by loopback Host Origin check plus a per-launch session token on state-changing requests via checkApiRequest in server-security. Untrusted 127.0.0.1:8788 is the ONLY thing the Tailscale sidecar reverse-proxies already-owner-gated remote traffic to; gated by a per-boot shared secret the sidecar stamps on every forwarded request checkRemoteApiRequest plus the session token on writes. The shared secret is a CSPRNG value generated once per launch in setupRemoteAccess, passed to the sidecar via environment variable never argv because argv is world-readable in the process table. The untrusted listener REQUIRES the secret so a local process or DNS-rebinding page without it fails closed. The trusted listener REFUSES the secret on any path before routing: a request carrying the sidecar secret is by definition sidecar-proxied remote traffic and has no business at the local door in createHandler.

sections.title: The Tailscale owner gate
sections.summary: The sidecar embeds Tailscale via tsnet and for every remote request calls WhoIs on the caller tailnet address, admitting only the studio owner's own account. Identity is compared by numeric user id who.UserProfile.ID equals Self.UserID via resolveOwnerID and newProxy; login-name strings are not used because tsnet can return an empty login for the owner node while the numeric id is populated. Fail closed everywhere: unresolved owner id zero denies everyone; unidentifiable caller with no WhoIs is denied; a caller whose node has no stable id is denied because a device that cannot be tracked or kicked will not be served. Identity headers forwarded upstream X-Tailscale-User and X-Tailscale-Node are taken from WhoIs never from client-supplied headers so a forged header cannot survive. These properties are unit-tested against a fake resolver in sidecar main_test.go.

sections.title: The LAN gate: connect code + per-device approval
sections.summary: Without tailnet identity, LAN gates on two stranger-proof checks in lan-host. Connect code the owner reads off screen is CSPRNG with rejection sampling, argon2id-hashed via Bun.password, and never sent to the connecting device. Wrong guesses throttle per IP with exponential backoff never a global lockout. Right code makes a pending session served nothing until host approval; pending is capped per IP and expires after 15 minutes so the code alone cannot flood approvals or leave stale entries. Listener binds 0.0.0.0:8790 with self-signed TLS in lan-server so code and traffic never cross clear; cert puts LAN IP and loopback in subjectAltName, regenerates if cache misses current IP, private key chmod 600 best effort with Windows ACLs; owner verifies shown sha256 fingerprint. Nested why the session cookie is not Secure: approved cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax Path slash without Secure because self-signed is not a secure context in some browsers that silently drop Secure cookies.

children.title: Why the session cookie is not `Secure`
children.summary: The approved-session cookie is HttpOnly SameSite Lax Path slash with no Secure attribute in lan-server. The listener is HTTPS-only, but a self-signed cert is not a secure context in some browsers, which then silently DROP a Secure cookie and leave the device stuck re-entering the code forever. SameSite Lax lets the cookie ride the reload navigation; HttpOnly still stands.

sections.title: Host-only surface
sections.summary: Whether a device tailed in over Tailscale or was approved on the LAN, it may USE the studio but must never reach management or host control. isHostOnlyRoute in server-remote refuses for any remote or LAN-served handler every api/remote route that turns access on or off or kicks devices, api/open that opens a browser on the host, api/shutdown, api/restart, and settings writes. Those belong to the local owner alone.

sections.title: Kicking a device
sections.summary: The owner can remove any connected device from the host. Over Tailscale the app writes a kick command to the sidecar stdin; the sidecar blocklists that node stable id and denies it on the next request even though it is the owner own account via deviceTracker in main.go. On LAN the session is dropped.

sections.title: Where the sidecar binary comes from
sections.summary: The sidecar is compiled Go and is not inside Hoplight.exe. sidecarCandidates in server-remote checks three locations in order: the repository sidecar folder that bun sidecar/build.ts writes, a sidecar folder beside the running executable, and the aux-package cache where a requested download installs it. None present reports unavailable, its own RemotePhase distinct from off and error, because off is a switch the owner can flip and error invites a retry while a build with no helper can do neither; the panel says so up front and offers no Enable control instead of spawning a path that is not there. LAN mode needs no helper. The beside-the-executable candidate is load-bearing: deriving the path from import.meta.url alone is correct from source and meaningless once compiled, resolving onto the Bun virtual filesystem, so every packaged studio failed to start remote access and surfaced a raw uv_spawn ENOENT. Pinned by server-remote.test.ts.

sections.title: The aux package: fetching the helper on request
sections.summary: The helper is about 31 MB, so it ships as a release asset the owner fetches with an explicit click. A SHA-256 pin is the integrity control and it is committed in sidecar-pins.ts, pinned like a dependency: scripts/pin-sidecar.ts reads a release's published SHA256SUMS, re-downloads each asset to confirm it matches, and rewrites the module for review. Computing it during the build was the earlier design and it split the product in two, because only a CI-built binary carried a hash, so the download worked for packaged users and silently did not from source. Committing it works because the helper is not tied to an app version: the coupling is to the stdio protocol, not the version number, which is also why there is no staleness signal. Verification runs on bytes in memory before anything reaches the path the spawner reads, and the install renames from a sibling staging file, so no tampered or torn download leaves a runnable binary. HTTPS only with every hop inspected, the size cap applies while reading, and the routes are host-only.

sections.title: Sidecar lifecycle
sections.summary: The sidecar is a background process that speaks only over stdio pipes: status events out, kick commands in. It watches stdin; when the parent app dies stdin hits EOF and the sidecar exits so a crashed app never leaves an orphan carrying a stale secret. On startup the manager also sweeps any orphan from a prior run before spawning a fresh one via killOrphans in sidecar-manager. The binary is built as a Windows GUI-subsystem executable with bun sidecar/build.ts -H=windowsgui so spawning from the window-less packaged app never pops a console; parent-provided pipes still work as handles independent of any console. Spawns also pass windowsHide as a second layer.

sections.title: What is proven
sections.summary: The Tailscale owner gate and its fail-closed cases are unit-tested in sidecar main_test.go. The LAN code format, per-IP throttle, pending cap, and TTL are unit-tested in lan-host.test.ts. The trusted-port secret refusal and the host-only route block are tested at the handler in server-remote.test.ts, including that a guest cannot trigger a helper download. The three binary locations, the unavailable phase, and the refusal to persist an on that cannot happen are unit-tested there and in sidecar-manager.test.ts, with the packaged path resolution confirmed against a real compiled executable. Every aux-download refusal is unit-tested in aux-download.test.ts: pin mismatch, truncation, a non-GitHub or plain-http hop, a lookalike host, redirect loops, and a body exceeding the cap while streaming. The checksum reader that writes the committed pins is unit-tested in sidecar-pin-format.test.ts. That the release builds and uploads a helper for every pinned platform, and that every committed pin names an asset the release publishes, is pinned by ci-sidecar.test.ts, covering workflow shape only; the Go cross-builds succeeding is proven by a real release run. The LAN and Tailscale paths have been verified live end-to-end.
